clue.text: Turn out boy who has lost old saw

parts.note: to turn out (to be so) is to prove

indicators.note: a boy who has lost something has had a piece taken away, so letters are removed from his name

parts.note: Rob is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad who has mislaid an elderly saw is told to get out of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who has lost' takes the O (old) out of ROB, leaving RB; 'saw' is the noun for a saying, not the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: An old saw is a traditional saying, and a proverb is exactly such a maxim.

clue.text: Give warning of object left on top

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on top of another comes before it

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: A note about a thing left lying on the top.
explanation.definitionFit: To portend is to foreshadow or give warning of something to come.

clue.text: Developing the art, score in this way?

definitions.text: Developing the art, score in this way?

indicators.note: developing means being worked into a new form, so the letters rearrange

explanation.surface: Building art through a musical score this way.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: to orchestrate is to develop a score.
explanation.definitionFit: To orchestrate is to arrange music for an orchestra, working up a score.

clue.text: Rates badly, final letter being of inferior quality

indicators.note: badly means in a jumbled way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Poor rates with a last letter are second-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes a substitute that is inferior to the real thing.

clue.text: American woman's promise to provide cutter

parts.note: broad is US slang for a woman, plus the possessive S
giving your word is promising

explanation.surface: A woman from the US pledges to supply a knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadsword is a cutting sword with a wide blade.

clue.text: Stretch of river accommodating vessels

indicators.note: a thing accommodating others holds them inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a crossword favourite
pans are cooking vessels

explanation.surface: A length of river has room for boats to moor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessels' suggests boats, but it means pans; THE EXE is a river in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An expanse is a wide stretch of land, sea or sky.

clue.text: Calm when letters are read aloud

indicators.note: something read aloud is heard, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: two letters E, said as E's

explanation.surface: Quiet when the post is read to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are E's, which sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease is to calm or soothe.

clue.text: Rightly given approval at last for time in real estate

indicators.note: one thing given for another is a replacement

parts.note: property is real estate

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of approval

explanation.surface: Correctly approved in the end for a timeshare apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: L (last of approval) replaces T in PROPERTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Properly and rightly both mean in the correct way.

clue.text: Take forty winks, using soft, fluffy surface

explanation.definitionFit: A nap is a short sleep and also the pile on fabric.

clue.text: Heed advert for protection from racket

parts.note: to lend an ear is to heed
a plug is a promotion

explanation.surface: Listen to an advert for noise protection.
explanation.definitionFit: An earplug protects from noise, a racket.

clue.text: Reported source of danger for legendary bird

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, signalling a word said out loud

parts.note: a rock is a hazard to shipping

explanation.surface: A mythical bird is said to be a menace.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is the giant bird of Arabian legend, as in the tales of Sinbad.

clue.text: Exhibits 27? It attracts prolonged applause

parts.note: to exhibit is to show, here in the third person
a cross-reference to 27 across, a hat, and a topper is a top hat

explanation.surface: A display of hats wins a long ovation.
explanation.walkthrough: The number 27 stands for the answer to 27 across, a hat; TOPPER is another word for a top hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A showstopper is a performance so well received that the applause halts the show.

clue.text: Flat fish consumed finally at the end of the day

indicators.note: a thing consumed is swallowed up, so it ends up inside the other pieces

parts.note: flat means level or even
the ide is a freshwater fish, common in crosswords

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the little word at

explanation.surface: A flatfish gets eaten at last when the day closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed' puts T, the last letter of 'at', inside EVEN + IDE; 'Flat fish' reads as one creature but splits into flat (EVEN) and fish (IDE).
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, the close of the day.

clue.text: Show about girl without sweetheart

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: Val is a girl's name
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: A display concerning a young woman who has no lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: VAL goes round E, the heart of 'sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal something is to show it or make it known.

clue.text: Tudor flower-girl not unknown in biblical village

parts.note: Eliza Doolittle is the flower girl of Shaw's Pygmalion

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter is removed

parts.note: Bethany is a village near Jerusalem in the Gospels
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A Tudor flower seller is unknown in a Holy Land village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not unknown' looks like a double negative, but it says drop Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elizabethan era is part of the Tudor period.

clue.text: Priest raised in old Yorks area, once taking precedence

indicators.note: the priest is put in, placed inside the old Yorkshire area

parts.note: a Riding was one of the old divisions of Yorkshire

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend

explanation.surface: A clergyman put up in an old Yorkshire area takes priority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses REV to VER, which goes into O RIDING.
explanation.definitionFit: Overriding means more important than all else.

clue.text: Known facts given a little backing

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the pieces read in reverse

parts.note: a tad is a little bit

explanation.surface: Established facts get modest support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the whole run A + TAD round.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures already known and recorded.

clue.text: Going the rounds, like Sampson Brass's clerk?

definitions.meaning: spinning or turning round on a pivot
Dick Swiveller is clerk to the lawyer Sampson Brass in Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop, so acting like him is jokingly behaving in Swiveller fashion

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a playful coinage from the name Swiveller, flagged by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Swivelling means turning round on a pivot, which is going round.

clue.text: One who enrolled soldiers after attending match

indicators.note: after places the next piece behind those before

parts.note: at means present at
a test is a cricket match
OR stands for other ranks

explanation.surface: Someone who signed up soldiers after watching a game.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to enrol in military service, so an attestor enrolled.

clue.text: They provide the key that secures their coats

definitions.text: They provide the key that secures their coats

parts.words: They provide the key that secures their coats
parts.note: reads like locksmiths or cloakroom attendants, but the key is the rough surface that holds a layer of render, and the coats are layers applied to walls

explanation.walkthrough: In building, the 'key' is the roughened surface that lets a coat of plaster grip.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradesmen who apply plaster first prepare a key so their coats of plaster adhere.

clue.text: Main steam locomotive?

definitions.meaning: the main is the open ocean

explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific is the largest ocean, and a type of steam engine.

clue.text: Graduate, perhaps? A sticky situation if one is pretty

definitions.meaning: to graduate is one example of succeeding in an exam or course

definitions.text: sticky situation if one is pretty
definitions.meaning: a pretty ... is a difficult state of affairs

explanation.walkthrough: 'A pretty pass' is an idiom for an awkward predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass is to succeed in an exam, which graduating exemplifies; a pretty pass is an idiomatic plight.

clue.text: Unscrupulous lawyer's timid way with queen

parts.note: shy is timid
St is short for street
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A crooked lawyer is timid with the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link meaning is.
explanation.definitionFit: A shyster is a disreputable lawyer.

clue.text: Partition, for example, erected across stream

indicators.note: across means spread around, so one piece wraps the other
in a down clue erected means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: eg means for example
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A partition built across a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected' turns EG to GE, which goes across RILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A grille is a grating that screens off a space.

clue.text: Adroit Conservative with means of exerting pressure

parts.note: a lever applies force

explanation.surface: A skilful Tory knows how to apply leverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit and clever are synonyms for skilful.

clue.text: Savagely penned expression of disgust, caught in bank

parts.note: fie is a written exclamation of disgust

indicators.note: something caught in another is held inside it

parts.note: to bank on is to rely
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone writes a furious complaint about being trapped in a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside RELY to give RCELY after FIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To act fiercely is to act savagely, with ferocity.

clue.text: Old Indo-European honey and spice drink, say

indicators.note: say, as in 'so to speak', means the word is to be spoken, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: mead is fermented honey

explanation.surface: An ancient person sips mead.
explanation.definitionFit: The Medes were an ancient Indo-European people.

clue.text: For a pelican, fish might be adequate

definitions.meaning: fish could stock a pelican's large pouched beak
to be suitable or good enough

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: a pelican's bill is filled with fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill the bill is an idiom for being just what is needed.

clue.text: Abraham's nephew's fate

definitions.meaning: in Genesis the man of Sodom

explanation.definitionFit: Lot was Abraham's nephew, and one's lot is one's destiny.

clue.text: Some relish a tasty pork pie, for example

indicators.note: some of the words means just a part of them is taken

explanation.surface: Part of a tasty pork pie is enjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: A pork pie is a flat-crowned hat as well as the food.
explanation.definitionFit: A pork pie is a style of hat with a flat crown.

clue.text: Select group's anger about being lodged in shed

indicators.note: being lodged in means placed inside

parts.note: a cote is a shed for doves or sheep

indicators.note: about here means turned round

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: A clique is furious about being housed in an outbuilding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses IRE to ERI, which goes inside COTE; the 's is a link meaning is.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive circle of people.

clue.text: Novelist initially rather more environment-conscious

parts.note: Graham Greene was an English novelist

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A writer is a little more eco-friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means environmentally aware, and greener is its comparative.
